previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fevers, lethargy, and a productive cough after a recent clinic visit, where he was found to have a urinary tract infection. He has a complex history including multiple myeloma, atrial fibrillation on warfarin, and a neobladder from prior bladder cancer. Admission labs showed acute kidney injury with a creatinine of 1.4, likely due to dehydration, and a urinalysis with high white blood cells. Urine culture confirmed VRE, and he was treated with IV daptomycin, later transitioned to oral linezolid. He developed oral ulcers during admission, managed with acyclovir. His renal function improved with IV fluids, and he received a transfusion for anemia. INR remained subtherapeutic but stable, so warfarin was continued without dose change. He remained afebrile, with resolving symptoms, and was discharged home on antibiotics and adjusted medications with close follow-up planned.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old man with a history of multiple 
myeloma s/p AutoSCT in ___ with disease recurrence in ___ 
treated with Velcade/Cytoxan/Dexamethasone in ___ who 
presents with concern for disseminated zoster.  

# Disseminated Zoster: Patient noted to have VZV about 1 week 
ago in the left T5 distribution prior to admission and had been 
taking oral Acyclovir since then, however, during a clinic 
visit, he demonstrated possible new lesions on his left flank 
and thigh sparing mucosal areas so he was admitted for concern 
of disseminated zoster. On initial examination, his zoster had 
not appeared to have spread beyond the left T5 dermatome and the 
other possible areas of involvement were consistent with 
hemangiomas. However, out of concern for possible dissemination, 
he was placed on precautions and administered IV Acyclovir 800mg 
q8H for the next 4 days. His rash remained stable, so he was 
discharged on Acyclovir 800mg five times days PO x 1 week with 
close oncology follow-up. He was also discharged on Gabapentin 
600mg TID for post-herpetic neuralgia. 
  
# Multiple myeloma: Patient is currently undergoing 
Velcade/Cytoxan/Dexamethasone treatment that he has been 
tolerating well. His cell counts were monitored daily as an 
inpatient and he did not require transfusion during his stay. 

# COPD: Patient without baseline O2 requirement and sat'ing well 
on room air on presentation, but diffusely wheezy with 
occasional cough on admission. His last PFT's in ___ 
demonstrated FEV1/FVC 82% of predicted, so he was continued on 
his home Advair 250 mcg-50 mcg 1 puff inh twice a day & 
Tiotropium 18mcg daily. He also received Albuterol nebs as an 
inpatient that improved his wheezing.  
  
# CAD s/p MI ___ with PCI to RCA: Patient on Toprol XL 25mg PO 
daily, but no other cardiac medications including a statin for 
unclear reasons. He was continued on his home Toprol XL 25mg PO 
daily.  

# Atrial Fibrillation: Coumadin dose currently on hold, per OSH 
providers. Patient continued on Toprol XL 25mg PO daily for rate 
control.  
  
# Hypertension: Continued Toprol XL 25mg PO daily  

# Depression: Continued Citalopram 60mg daily
